rules.reason: Appears to guarantee a financial, tax, savings, or income outcome. The spec forbids tax, legal, income, profit, savings, and rate guarantees outright.
rules.notes: Co-occurrence rather than a single phrase: 'guaranteed' alone is fine ('guaranteed to be organized'), and 'save' alone is fine. The pair is what creates the claim.

rules.reason: Appears to guarantee a spiritual outcome. The spec forbids guaranteeing spiritual outcomes and forbids claiming religious authority.
Claims religious authority or issues a ruling. The spec forbids claiming religious authority and requires founder approval before citing any ayah, hadith, fatwa, or scholarly position.
rules.notes: Fires on Rig Receipts content too. A religious ruling appearing on the trucking brand would be at least as serious as on Tilawah Lock.

rules.reason: Uses guilt, shame, or religious pressure. The spec forbids shaming Muslims and forbids exploiting religious guilt.
patterns: \b(?:shame on you|you should be ashamed|be ashamed)\b

rules.reason: Makes payment feel religiously obligatory. The spec forbids making payment feel religiously forced.
rules.notes: Ordinary premium messaging is Yellow, not Red — see YEL-TL-PAYWALL-WORSHIP. This rule fires only when the pitch ties payment to religious sincerity.

rules.reason: Positions Rig Receipts as a load board or implies booking, bidding, dispatching, or contacting brokers. The spec states Rig Receipts is not a load board.
Names a specific freight broker. The spec forbids publishing broker names in general public examples.
patterns: \b(?:c\.?h\.? ?robinson|chrobinson|total quality logistics|\btql\b|xpo logistics|coyote logistics|landstar|echo global|rxo|uber freight|convoy|jb ?hunt|j\.?b\.? hunt|schneider logistics|worldwide express|arcbest|nolan transportation|ntg logistics|england logistics|allen lund|gp transco)\b
rules.notes: Starter denylist of publicly-known brokerages. Extend as needed; an unlisted broker name still trips YEL-RR-BROKER because the word 'broker' will almost always appear alongside it.

rules.reason: References real freight paperwork with identifying detail. The spec forbids using real sensitive freight paperwork in public marketing and requires public rate-card examples to be fictional or privacy-redacted.
patterns: \b(?:actual|real|my own|my|our|this week's|last week's|attached) (?:\w+ )?(?:rate con(?:firmation)?|bol|bill of lading|load confirmation|pro number|scale ticket)s?\b
\bscreenshot of (?:a |the |my |our )?(?:\w+ )?(?:rate con(?:firmation)?|bol|bill of lading|load confirmation|pro number|scale ticket)s?\b
\b(?:rate con(?:firmation)?|bol|bill of lading|load confirmation|pro number|scale ticket)s? from (?:my|our|a real|an actual|last week's|this week's)\b
rules.notes: Proximity patterns, not document-wide co-occurrence: an early version matched any post containing both 'rate con' and a generic 'real' anywhere, which blocked clean educational copy ('the real number'). The actual-ness term must sit against the paperwork term. The none_of clause is what lets a properly-labelled fictional example through.

rules.reason: Encourages unsafe or non-compliant trucking behavior. The spec forbids this outright.
References private APIs, scraping, or automation intended to evade platform restrictions. The spec forbids all of these.
States a statistic as fact without a source. The spec forbids using unverified statistics as fact.
all_of: \b(?:studies show|research shows|statistics show|data shows|it(?:'s| is) proven|proven that|fact:|the average \w+)\b
rules.notes: Deliberately narrow: a bare percentage does not fire on its own, only a percentage presented with authority language and no source marker.
